ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A rectangular paper $MNPQ$ is folded in the manner shown such that vertex $Q$ coincides with $N$, with the fold line being $AB$, $MN=3$, and $MQ=9$. What is the length of the fold line $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect NQ as shown in the diagram:\\
Since quadrilateral MNPQ is a rectangle,\\
thus, $\angle M=90^\circ$, $PN\parallel MQ$,\\
thus, $NQ=\sqrt{MN^2+MQ^2}=\sqrt{3^2+9^2}=3\sqrt{10}$,\\
According to the folding, AB is perpendicular bisector of NQ,\\
thus, $\angle QOA=\angle M=90^\circ$,\\
$OQ=ON=\frac{1}{2}NQ=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}$,\\
Since $\angle AQO=\angle NOM$,\\
thus, $\triangle AQO\sim \triangle NQM$,\\
thus, $\frac{AO}{MN}=\frac{OQ}{MQ}$,\\
which means $\frac{AO}{3}=\frac{\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}}{9}$,\\
thus, $AO=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$,\\
Since $PN\parallel MQ$,\\
thus, $\angle AQO=\angle BNO$,\\
Since in $\triangle AQO$ and $\triangle BNO$
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle AQO=\angle BNO \\
OQ=ON \\
\angle AOQ=\angle BON
\end{array}\right.$,\\
thus, $\triangle AQO\cong \triangle BNO$,\\
thus, AO=BO,\\
thus, $AB=2AO=2\times \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}=\boxed{\sqrt{10}}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate geometry route. From the image, orient the rectangle with MQ vertical and MN horizontal, and read that A is where the crease meets the left side MQ while B is where it meets the right side NP. Put Q=(0,0), M=(0,9), P=(3,0), and N=(3,9), using MN=3 and MQ=9 from the text. Since folding maps Q to N, the crease AB is the perpendicular bisector of segment QN. Segment QN has slope 9/3=3 and midpoint O=(3/2,9/2), so AB has slope -1/3 and equation y-9/2=-(1/3)(x-3/2), i.e. y=5-x/3. Intersect this line with x=0 to get A=(0,5), and with x=3 to get B=(3,4). Then AB=sqrt((3-0)^2+(4-5)^2)=sqrt(10).

raw_record.original_question: A rectangular paper $MNPQ$ is folded in the manner shown such that vertex $Q$ coincides with $N$, with the fold line being $AB$, $MN=3$, and $MQ=9$. What is the length of the fold line $AB$?
raw_record.answer: Connect $NQ$ as shown in the diagram. Since quadrilateral $MNPQ$ is a rectangle, $\angle M=90^\circ$ and $PN\parallel MQ$. Thus, $NQ=\sqrt{MN^2+MQ^2}=\sqrt{3^2+9^2}=3\sqrt{10}$. According to the folding, $AB$ is the perpendicular bisector of $NQ$. Thus, $\angle QOA=\angle M=90^\circ$, and $OQ=ON=\frac{1}{2}NQ=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}$. Since $\angle AQO=\angle NOM$, $\triangle AQO\sim\triangle NQM$. Therefore, $\frac{AO}{MN}=\frac{OQ}{MQ}$, so $\frac{AO}{3}=\frac{\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}}{9}$, giving $AO=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}$. Since $PN\parallel MQ$, $\angle AQO=\angle BNO$. In $\triangle AQO$ and $\triangle BNO$, we have $\angle AQO=\angle BNO$, $OQ=ON$, and $\angle AOQ=\angle BON$, so $\triangle AQO\cong\triangle BNO$. Hence $AO=BO$, and $AB=2AO=2\times\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}=\boxed{\sqrt{10}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, in the original rectangle MNPQ, M and N are above, and Q and P are below, represented by dashed lines; A is located on the left side MQ, B is located on the right side NP, and AB is the crease. After folding, Q coincides with N, the corresponding point of the lower-right vertex P is marked as P′, and the figure also reflects that MQ and NP are parallel. Reasoning: Connect NQ, and let NQ intersect the crease AB at O. Because MNPQ is a rectangle, MN = 3, MQ = 9, and ∠M = 90°, so in the right triangle MNQ, NQ = √(3² + 9²) = 3√10. The folding makes Q coincide with N, therefore the crease AB is the perpendicular bisector of NQ, so OQ = ON = 3√10/2, and AB ⟂ NQ. By the perpendicular and parallel relationships of the rectangle sides, △AQO and △NQM are similar, so AO/MN = OQ/MQ. Substituting gives AO/3 = (3√10/2)/9, so AO = √10/2. Also because MQ ∥ NP, and OQ and ON are on the same straight line NQ, combined with OQ = ON and AB ⟂ NQ, it can be obtained that △AQO and △BNO are correspondingly congruent, therefore AO = BO. Thus AB = AO + BO = 2AO = √10.
